label: prop:terminal-resolution
title: Terminal Resolution of Hadronic Mass
html:
The hadronic mass collapses into a combination of neutrino vacuum drag and pure strong-force binding energy. Absolute nucleon mass in MeV is not itself a framework prediction: m_e fixes the MeV scale by fiat, so the predictive content is the dimensionless ratio, and the proton and neutron entries below are that ratio rendered against the m_e unit. What the substrate parameter q_0 predicts is the isospin splitting, and the accompanying proof reaches m_n - m_p at a -0.53\% residual — about 6.9\,\text{keV}. The deuteron and binding-energy rows are tabulated for orientation; neither is derived here, and the binding row sits 1\,\text{keV} from CODATA at the precision shown.

Structure Topological Formula QOU Result (MeV) CODATA (MeV)
Proton (m_p) Q(q) \mathfrak{m}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}})_{uud} 938.272 938.272
Neutron (m_n) Q(q) \mathfrak{m}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}})_{udd} 939.565 939.565
Deuteron (m_D) \mathfrak{m}(L_6) - \text{Binding} 1875.613 1875.613
Binding Energy \Delta Skein Polynomial 2.224 2.225

The formula column and the accompanying proof are two different routes to the same two rows. The column states the proton and neutron as Q(q) applied to a Hopf-link mass; the proof derives them as sums over Skein crossing pairs, m_p = \mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}} + 2\mathcal{S}_{\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}}, from dressed quark masses \mu_{\mathfrak{u}} \approx 311.10 and \mu_{\mathfrak{d}} \approx 312.39\,\text{MeV}. The residual quoted above is the proof's. The two routes are not shown here to agree.
